key_insight: HSE introduced a practical screened-hybrid exchange strategy that made exact exchange affordable in solids and unexpectedly delivered much better band gaps than semilocal DFT for many semiconductors.
engineering_relevance: The work matters for materials and device design because accurate, transferable band gaps are critical for predicting defects, photovoltaics, power electronics, and quantum-information materials.
method: Keep exact exchange at short range and screen it at long range.
Use a fixed 25% exchange fraction inherited from PBE0 rather than fitting to solids.
Compare HSE03/HSE06 and newer semilocal, meta-GGA, and dielectric-dependent/tuned hybrids against solid benchmarks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that HSE band gaps for ordinary semiconductors and selected metal oxides came out substantially closer to experiment than conventional semilocal approximations, and recent meta-GGAs can reach HSE06-level accuracy for selected semiconductors.
watch_item: Fixed screening and exchange fractions improve practicality, but transferability can still fail across materials with different dielectric environments, so tuned or dielectric-dependent hybrids may be needed.
paper_title: Perspective: The HSE Screened Hybrid and the Band Gap Problem: Origins, Impact, and the Contenders
